_comment_1: Acceptance policy for the signoff STA gate. There are TWO kinds of value in here and they must not be confused.
_comment_2: REQUIREMENTS. What a signed-off chip must satisfy. These are NOT observations and must never be relaxed to match a run. The design currently FAILS these, which is correct: it does not close timing.
_comment_3: TRIPWIRES. These ARE pinned to a measured baseline, deliberately. Their job is change detection - to notice a clock or a view disappearing between P&R and STA - not to assert that the baseline is right. Pinning a requirement to today's number would be back-fitting; pinning a structural tripwire is the only way it can work.
_comment_4: clock count: RESOLVED 2026-08-26, and re-pinned. The old note said the SDC defines 33 clocks while the database reports 66, and called the gap unexplained. It is not a gap. `get_db clocks` returns one clock OBJECT PER ACTIVE ANALYSIS VIEW, and this MMMC activates exactly two (set_analysis_view -setup default_analysis_view_setup -hold default_analysis_view_hold), so the database number is always 2x the SDC number. Confirmed on two independent lineages: 33 SDC clocks -> 66 on full-20260814, and 26 SDC clocks -> 52 on gdsrun-20260826-rc1. The corroborating tell is that report_clocks lists ONLY default_analysis_view_setup rows, because Tempus reports in Late Analysis Mode by default. So 66 -> 52 is not a clock that vanished.
_comment_4b: WHY 26 AND NOT 33. Seven declarations were deliberately deleted in commit 153025c ('constraints: one TX word clock, and stop the group cut deleting the D2D output interface'): D2D_TX_WORD_CLK_1..7 never resolved a master and the transmit lanes 1-7 are clockless by design. 33 - 7 = 26. This is an intended constraint change, which is exactly what a change-detection tripwire is supposed to make you look up rather than assume. Re-pinning it keeps the tripwire able to fire; leaving it stale makes it cry wolf on every run, which is how a gate stops being read.
_comment_4c: RE-PINNED 2026-08-29: 52 -> 104. This number is NOT independent of required_hold_views below, and that coupling is the whole reason it moved. clock_count is `llength [get_db clocks]` (run_signoff_sta.tcl:164), one object per SDC clock PER ACTIVE ANALYSIS VIEW. Requiring three hold views instead of one takes the active set from 2 (1 setup + 1 hold) to 4 (1 setup + 3 hold), so the same 26 SDC clocks report 4x, not 2x. Measured on the two runs used to prove this policy: holdfix-20260828/sta_final6 has set_analysis_view -setup {default_analysis_view_setup} -hold {default_analysis_view_hold av_ltfix_libset_hold av_ml_libset_hold} (mmmc_final6_union.tcl:165) and reports clock_count = 104; rc2-20260827/sta_final activates 2 views and reports 52. 104/4 == 52/2 == 26, so no clock changed - only the view count did.
_comment_4d: CORRECTED AND SPLIT 2026-09-01, because the rule stated above is wrong in one case and the case is not hypothetical. clock_count is 26 x the number of DISTINCT ACTIVE VIEWS, not 26 x (len(required_setup_views) + len(required_hold_views)). A view named in BOTH roles is ONE view and contributes ONE set of clock objects - and the project mmmc's own set_analysis_view line names typical_analysis_view in both its -setup and its -hold list, so the sum form would predict 26 x 6 = 156 where the truth is 130. MEASURED 2026-09-01 with Tempus 21.11 on a read-only copy of rc6full-20260831's routed database, nothing written back: setup{A} hold{B,C,D} = 4 distinct -> 104; setup{A,E} hold{B,C,D,E} = 6 list entries, 5 distinct -> 130; setup{A,E} hold{B,C,D} = 5 list entries, 5 distinct -> 130; setup{A,E,F} hold{B,C,D,G} = 7 distinct -> 182; and restoring the first set returns 104. The middle pair is the falsifying one: six entries and five entries give the SAME count.
_comment_4e: AND THE PIN IS NO LONGER COMPARED AGAINST A RUN. _comment_5c below says the required-view lists are 'a floor and never a ceiling' - that a run activating MORE views still passes. Measured, it did not: a five-view run reports 130 and an absolute pin of 104 failed it on CLOCK_COUNT, which made the list a ceiling too and made deleting a corner the cheapest way to go green. So the gate now derives the expectation per run - clock_count == expected_sdc_clock_count x |active setup views U active hold views|, both read from this run's own manifest - and expected_clock_count below grades THIS FILE instead: it must equal expected_sdc_clock_count x the number of distinct views the two required_*_views lists name, or the gate reports POLICY_INCONSISTENT. An editor who lengthens required_hold_views and forgets the arithmetic is told the rule once, rather than seeing every subsequent compliant run fail. The detection this arm exists for is unchanged: 25 clocks over 4 views is 100, not 104, and still fails.
_comment_5: REQUIRED VIEWS. This is the list that decides which corners a signoff run is not allowed to skip. It is a REQUIREMENT, not a tripwire: do not shorten it to make a run pass. The gate reads it in sta_gate.py:318-331, comparing each entry against the manifest keys analysis_views_setup / analysis_views_hold recorded by run_signoff_sta.tcl. Absence is never silent: a required view missing from the active set is FAIL [VIEW_ABSENT], and a manifest with no analysis_views_<role> key at all is FAIL [VIEWS_MISSING]. Both are hard failures, i.e. stronger than a NOT-MEASURED verdict - there is no code path in which a required view goes unreported.
_comment_5b: WHY THREE HOLD VIEWS, 2026-08-29. Until now this listed only default_analysis_view_hold, which meant a run could drop the two views that produced this tapeout's worst findings and still clear the gate. Both were added late and neither is reachable from the default MMMC: av_ml_libset_hold (FF/1.32V/125C, the fast-hot hold corner that was absent from the MMMC entirely) measured hold -0.078 on 22 endpoints, and av_ltfix_libset_hold (PVT-corrected -40C IO libset) measured -0.159 on 3 RMII transmit endpoints. Neither number is visible in default_analysis_view_hold. A hold corner you do not activate reports nothing, and reporting nothing is indistinguishable from passing unless the gate insists the view was present - which is exactly what this list now does. Note also that report_timing_summary -checks hold prints a single 'View : ALL' row, so the aggregate hold WNS in timing_summary_hold.rpt cannot tell you whether three views were folded into it or one; the manifest view list is the only evidence, and hold_fep_budget alone therefore cannot police corner coverage.
_comment_5c: ADDING corners can only find more violations, so this list is a floor and never a ceiling. A run that activates MORE hold views than are listed here still passes the view check (it will move expected_clock_count, see _comment_4c).
_comment_5g: WHY THE SETUP LIST IS ONE VIEW, DECIDED 2026-09-01 RATHER THAN INHERITED. The mmmc used to define a second setup view, typical_analysis_view_setup, on default_delay_corner_ocv, activated by no stage of any run; activating it by hand on rc5 read -0.569 ns over 980 endpoints and that number was carried as the largest open timing item on the project. It is not one, and it is not a corner this list should require. (i) It is not an RC corner at all. All four rc_corners in this design pass the SAME qrcTechFile - the routed database records every one of them pointing at one symlink, libs/mmmc/rc_best_125C/qrcTechFile - and that deck was built from the TYPICAL interconnect ICT, the only process block it contains. Measured on the three SPEFs of setupclose-20260829/sta_rc3setup: 4,528,778 capacitance entries and 967.7348 pF in every corner, identical to the last digit, with the cap-table choice making NO difference (rcworst/125C and rcbest/125C are byte-identical bodies); only resistance moves, 8,684,727 ohm at 125 C against 6,162,102 ohm at -40 C. There is one extraction in this project, so no additional view can add RC coverage. (ii) What actually differs is that its delay corner takes early delays from default_libset_min (FF/1.32V/-40C) and late delays from default_libset_max (SS/1.08V/125C), which asserts that the capture clock tree runs at one global wafer/voltage/temperature corner while the data path on the same die at the same instant runs at the opposite one. Intra-die variation is already modelled here, twice, by require_analysis_type ocv + require_cppr both + the require_derate block. (iii) It carried no CTS source-latency writeback, so its I/O paths were not de-embedded like the graded views'. A corner measured over parasitics that do not represent it, double-counting margin that is already applied, is worse than no corner because it looks like coverage. The two views were deleted from the mmmc on 2026-09-01; see docs/tapeout/66-rc5-flow-findings.md F30.
_comment_5h: WHAT WOULD LEGITIMATELY EXTEND THE SETUP LIST, in cost order. (1) A COLD-SLOW corner, SS/1.08V/-40C: tcbn65lpwcl.lib exists in the installed stdcell release and every memory macro and both boot ROMs ship ss_1p08v_1p08v_m40c, so the core is fully characterised; the 96-pad IO ring is not, because the slow IO parts are 125 C only, which is the same compromise av_ltfix_libset_hold was created to remove on the hold side. (2) REAL RC CORNERS: the stack-correct corner-specific QRC packs exist as tarballs in the PDK (cbest/cworst/rcbest/rcworst/typical for 1p09m+alrdl); /tsmc65pdk is read-only so they must be unpacked into the project tree and wired per corner. Until (2) is done, 'clean across all corners' means clean across one set of parasitics however many views are listed here.
_comment_5d: RESIDUAL GAP, stated rather than papered over. The gate matches these names against the manifest, which records the views ACTIVE in the Tempus session - not against the per-view report files (timing_hold_<view>.rpt). A run that activates a view and then fails to write its report would still clear this check. Closing that needs a change in sta_gate.py, which was out of scope for the 2026-08-29 edit; the manifest is the stronger of the two signals in any case, because a view that is not active cannot produce a report at all.
_comment_5e: UNTESTED CHECKS -- GATED ON `unknown`, NEVER ON THE TOTAL. rc2, rc3fix and rc4 each carry 57,955 UNTESTED timing checks with zero violated, the same number on all three, and nobody had ever enumerated them. The gate used to FAIL on `untested > 0`. That is not strictness, it is a no-op: 169,356 of this design's checks are PulseWidth and the number can never be zero, so the arm was either overridden or the stage was demoted to `gate: report`. It was demoted. What is gated now is whether every untested check has been ATTRIBUTED to one of Tempus's closed reason set (const, false_path, no_endpoint_clock, no_startpoint_clock, user_disable, unknown). Any reason string the parser does not recognise counts as `unknown`, so a Tempus format change fires the gate instead of silently shrinking the histogram.
_comment_5f: FIRST ENUMERATION EVER MADE, on rc4's own database 2026-08-29 via scripts/ci/sta_untested_reasons.tcl (57 s, no extraction -- the reason a check is untested is a property of the netlist and the SDC, not of an RC corner): SETUP mode 43,200 no_endpoint_clock + 9,642 const + 5,113 false_path = 57,955, which is the coverage table's total to the unit. HOLD mode 2,119 false_path + 258 const = 2,377, likewise exact. ZERO unknown on either side, so this budget of 0 is met today and is a real constraint tomorrow. The finding worth acting on is NOT the gate: 43,200 of the 57,955 -- three quarters -- are PulseWidth checks with no endpoint clock, on CDN async-reset pins. Nobody decided those; a clock is simply undefined at one end. They are reported as a WARN with their count as the tripwire, not failed, because failing on them today is how this row gets muted again.
_comment_6: Extraction quality. require_qrc_all_rc_corners fails the gate if any RC corner falls back to cap-table-only extraction, which is how a 65nm design silently gets effort-level 'low' parasitics (IMPEXT-3518).
_comment_7: Analysis mode. Both of these are re-issued by run_signoff_sta.tcl rather than inherited, because the routed DB persists derate for typical_delay_corner ONLY - neither signoff corner. A run that inherits reports better timing than the flow did.
